This year I still won’t do anything fancy. I can’t read those technical things, so I go by what I’ve seen on my own land and what people around me do. Cotton is still my main crop, because on my small land it brings cash if the year is decent. But I also keep a little wheat and maize. Wheat and maize are steady, and if cotton price or weather goes bad, at least I still have grain. My land is only 4.1 mu, and some people in the family work outside, so I need a plan that does not cost too much and that we can manage ourselves. I have a well, so if the sky stays dry, I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I won’t water for nothing.

For cotton, I will keep the bigger piece, because that is the crop I know best and I’ve grown it many years. I’ll use the same local hybrid seed people nearby buy, not the expensive kind. Before planting I’ll put some base fertilizer, not too heavy because cash is tight, then if the plants look weak later I’ll add a bit more. Cotton takes more hand work, but with only a few mu I can still manage with family labor. For wheat and maize, I’ll keep a smaller area in the usual wheat-maize way on the same piece, because that is my backup. Wheat I’ll sow around October like always, give base fertilizer, then topdress once in spring if it looks yellow. After wheat harvest I’ll plant maize right away, no delay, because that summer window is short. Maize grows fast here, so I won’t spend too much on it, just enough fertilizer and one or two waterings if rain is poor.
